headline: Visiting the World's Smallest Desert Safely and Responsibly
reservation: No permits are required for day-use access to the Carcross Desert dunes, but organized groups or commercial filming require prior authorization from the Yukon government. If staying overnight in the region, accommodation in Carcross or Whitehorse must be secured well in advance as local capacity is extremely limited. Visitors must stay on established paths to protect the fragile local flora, including the rare Baikal Sedge.

days.title: Ancient Sands and First Nations Culture

stops.name: Carcross Desert Dunes
stops.detail: Walk the northern section of the 260-hectare sand deposit, a post-glacial remnant of an ancient lake bed.

stops.name: Carcross/Tagish First Nation Cultural Centre
stops.detail: Learn about the traditional territory and the significance of the 'Nares Cross' through local carvings and exhibits.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for the direct drive; conditions are generally clear in summer.
days.note: Footwear with good coverage is recommended as the sand can be surprisingly cold or hold debris.

days.title: Southern Lakes Panorama

stops.name: Nares Lake Shoreline
stops.detail: Observe the migratory bird patterns where the desert sands meet the riparian environment of the Southern Lakes.

stops.name: Emerald Lake Viewpoint
stops.detail: Located just north of the desert, this stop offers views of intense calcium-carbonate-induced colors in the water.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes of total transit; stops are very close to one another.
days.note: The Emerald Lake viewpoint is a popular pull-off; exercise caution when pulling back onto the highway.

days.title: South Klondike Exploration

stops.name: White Pass & Yukon Route Station
stops.detail: View the historic rail architecture that defines the gateway between the coast and the interior desert.

stops.name: Conrad Ghost Town
stops.detail: Drive south to see the remains of the early 20th-century silver mining boom along the windy shores of Windy Arm.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours for return travel; high winds are common in this corridor.
days.note: Conrad involves a short walk from the highway; ensure vehicles are parked fully off the shoulder.

intel.title: Desert Pull-out
intel.text: A small paved parking area is located directly off the South Klondike Highway at the desert's edge. It can fill quickly midday, so consider visiting during off-peak morning hours.

intel.title: Carcross Area Reception
intel.text: Expect basic LTE coverage in the town of Carcross and at the desert dunes. Signal strength drops significantly as you move toward the mountains.

intel.title: Gateway Provisions
intel.text: Gas is available in Carcross, but prices are often lower in Whitehorse. Confirm station hours if traveling on Sundays or late in the evening.

intel.title: Optimal Dune Lighting
intel.text: Early morning offers the best contrast on the sand ripples before the high sun flattens the landscape. Midday heat is rare but the sand reflects significant UV rays.

intel.title: Fragile Ecosystem Limits
intel.text: Motorized vehicles are strictly prohibited on the dunes to protect endemic plant species. Pedestrian access is permitted but hikers should avoid trampling visible vegetation.

plan.arrival: After landing at YXY, pick up a rental and head south on the Alaska Highway before turning onto the South Klondike Highway toward Carcross.
plan.vehicle: The route is fully paved and accessible to all vehicle types, including large RVs, though parking at the desert is tight for trailers.
plan.goldenHour: The dunes at the Carcross Desert catch the late evening light beautifully, with the surrounding mountains providing a stark backdrop.
